Kanawha County by the numbers

Kanawha County ranks 1 of 13 West Virginia counties in this guide by population, at about 178,198 people in 90,388 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $135,000, the median home value sits 15% below the West Virginia county median for this guide. The West Virginia county median income is $58,326, and Kanawha County reports $58,887. Owner-occupancy is 70%, so renters hold about 30% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1966, about 57 years ago.

Where is Kanawha County and how is its property tax organized?

Kanawha County is in south-central West Virginia, and its county seat is Charleston, which is also the state capital. The county was formed in 1789 and covers 911 square miles, of which about 902 are land. Interstates 64, 77 and 79 all pass through it, along with U.S. 60 and U.S. 119.

Inside the county you will find the cities of Charleston, Dunbar, Marmet, St. Albans and South Charleston, plus parts of Nitro, Montgomery and Smithers. Smaller towns such as Belle, Cedar Grove, Clendenin and Pratt sit along the river valleys. Kanawha County also runs on four magisterial districts. Which of these places your house is in decides whether the municipal levy applies to it, and that changes the bill.

How does the Kanawha County Sheriff bill and collect property tax?

The Sheriff's Tax Office mails statements by July 15 each year, and the sheriff, not the assessor, collects the money. The office says taxpayers avoid interest by paying the first half before October 1 and the second half by April 1. The state's own calendar also lists September 1 and March 1 as the installment dates that earn the 2.5 percent discount.

Payments can be made several ways. The office accepts Visa, Mastercard and Discover by phone during business hours at 304-357-0210, and you need the eight digit account number printed in small type at the top right of your statement. Mailed checks go to 409 Virginia St E, Room 120, Charleston, WV 25301, with the account number on the memo line.

  • Statements go out by July 15 and are based on ownership as of the prior July 1.
  • Personal property bills run a year behind, so a vehicle you sold can still appear on a statement.
  • Lost statements can be replaced by phone, and an online tax inquiry link is on the sheriff's website.
  • Address changes go through the Assessor's Office, not the sheriff.

For a seller this matters in one practical way: a statement that never reached a vacant or inherited house is still a lien-bearing debt. Check the online inquiry before you list or accept any offer.

What happens when real estate tax goes unpaid in Kanawha County?

Unpaid tax first turns into interest at 9 percent a year, and later into a tax lien that can be sold. State rules say the first half becomes delinquent on October 1 and the second half on April 1. The sheriff's collection page says about 100,000 tickets exist at the start of a year and that roughly 92 percent of current-year tax is collected within the first 10 months.

That page also describes an annual November sale of about 2,100 delinquent liens, bringing in roughly $2.5 million to $3.0 million. Be aware that the Marion County Sheriff and the Jefferson County website now say the Legislature moved the sale of delinquent real estate liens to the State Auditor. Kanawha's page has not caught up in its wording, so ask the Sheriff's Tax Office who runs the sale for your parcel and what the redemption steps are.

The collection unit also tracks bad checks, bankruptcy claims and the county hotel and motel tax. A homeowner who is behind on tax and also in bankruptcy should expect the office to file a claim.

How do you challenge a Kanawha County assessment?

You file a protest with the county commission, which sits as the Board of Equalization and Review beginning February 1 and must finish by the end of February. West Virginia law lets the board adjourn any time after February 15 once its work is done. If you skip this window, you generally waive the right to question that year's list except by appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals.

The board looks at value, not at what a house is. If it finds property assessed at more or less than 60 percent of true and actual value, it fixes the assessment at 60 percent, and it cannot raise a value without five days of written notice. Questions about classification or taxability go a different route, to the assessor and then the Tax Commissioner. A house wrongly placed in Class IV when it is owner-occupied is a classification matter.

  • Kanawha County Assessor: 409 Virginia Street E., Charleston. The sheriff's FAQ gives 304-357-0250 for assessment questions.
  • Appeal from the board's order goes to the Office of Tax Appeals, filed by March 31 of the tax year.
  • The standard of proof is a preponderance of the evidence.
  • Recent sale prices, repair estimates and photos of defects are the usual evidence.

What did the 2016 flood change for Kanawha County houses?

The June 2016 flood left a long mark on the county's river-valley neighborhoods. The National Weather Service reports that on June 23, 2016, heavy thunderstorms caused flash flooding across West Virginia, with 23 deaths statewide, including 6 in Kanawha County. Its photo record shows flooding in Clendenin and Elkview, where a bridge collapsed.

Geography explains why. The Kanawha River forms at Gauley Bridge and is joined by the Elk River in Charleston, according to a regional hazard mitigation plan. A State of Emergency was declared in 44 of the state's 55 counties that month.

If you own a house that took water, still has damaged floors or has a roof and furnace that need work, you face a decision. Repairing and listing on the open market takes time and cash, and a buyer's lender may balk at condition. A cash buyer who purchases as-is lets you skip that repair cycle, and you still settle taxes from the proceeds.

What taxes and costs come up when selling a Kanawha County house for cash?

Expect to settle delinquent property tax, a transfer tax and any liens out of the proceeds. West Virginia charges an excise tax on recorded deeds, and the statute adds a county excise tax of 55 cents for each $500 of value. Transfers of $1,000 or less in value are excluded from the definition.

The regular ceiling for an owner-occupied Class II home inside a municipality adds up to $1.00 per $100 of assessed value: 0.50 cents state, 28.60 county, 45.90 schools and 25.00 municipal, in cents per $100. As an illustration, a $120,000 house assessed at 60 percent is $72,000, which gives $720 at that ceiling before any voter-approved excess levies. Kanawha County does carry an excess levy, so the real figure can run higher. Rental and vacant property can fall in Class III or IV, where ceilings are higher.

  • Owners 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, may exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value.
  • The exemption needs West Virginia residency for the two prior calendar years.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff of any unpaid tickets before closing.

Selling a house in Kanawha County with tax due, repairs or tenants

Most sellers we hear from in Kanawha County are not pricing a perfect home. They are dealing with an inherited house in Charleston, a rental in St. Albans with a tenant who will not leave, or a property with tax tickets in arrears. We buy houses as-is in cash, so tax can be paid at closing and you do not need to clean out, repair or stage the house. Call or text (424) 435-2326 for a written offer, and compare it with any other.

More questions about Kanawha County, WV Property Tax Guide

When are Kanawha County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before each date. The Sheriff's Tax Office says to pay the first half before October 1 and the second by April 1 to avoid interest.

How much interest does Kanawha County charge on late tax?

Delinquent West Virginia property tax accrues interest at 9 percent a year. First-half tax becomes delinquent on October 1 and second-half tax on April 1.

Who do I call about a Kanawha County tax bill?

Call the Sheriff's Tax Office at 304-357-0210 for bills and payments. The sheriff's FAQ lists 304-357-0250 for the Assessor's Office on address changes and assessment questions.

Can I sell a Kanawha County house if the taxes are unpaid?

Yes. Unpaid tax is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the sheriff or title company for a current payoff first.

What is the deadline to protest a Kanawha County assessment?

The county commission meets as the Board of Equalization and Review from February 1 and must adjourn by the end of February. An appeal from its order to the Office of Tax Appeals is due by March 31.

Cabell County by the numbers

Cabell County ranks 4 of 13 West Virginia counties in this guide by population, at about 93,300 people in 46,084 housing units (Census Bureau, 2019-2023). At $156,100, the median home value sits 2% below the West Virginia county median for this guide. The West Virginia county median income is $58,326, and Cabell County reports $52,828. Owner-occupancy is 64%, so renters hold about 36% of occupied homes. The median home was built in 1969, about 54 years ago.

Where is Cabell County and how is it laid out?

Cabell County sits on the Ohio River in the southwestern corner of West Virginia, and Huntington is its county seat. The county covers 288 square miles, 281 of them land, according to the Census Bureau figures summarized on Wikipedia. Huntington itself extends partly into Wayne County.

East of Huntington you find the city of Milton and the village of Barboursville, plus the census-designated places of Culloden and Lesage. Interstate 64, U.S. 52, U.S. 60 and state routes 2, 10, 152 and 527 carry most of the traffic. Across the river lie Gallia and Lawrence counties in Ohio.

Cabell had 94,350 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 91,183 in 2025. County government runs five numbered magisterial districts, yet the old district names and boundaries were kept as tax and assessment districts. That detail shows up on a tax ticket, so a seller should know which district the parcel falls in.

What drives the Cabell County economy?

Education, manufacturing, transportation and government carry the Cabell County economy. The West Virginia Encyclopedia calls Marshall University one of the county's largest employers and notes that the International Nickel Company plant opened in 1921. Special Metals, a nickel alloy producer, lists its Huntington plant at 3200 Riverside Drive with two 70,000 pound electric arc furnaces.

Blenko Glass has operated in Milton since 1921, and CSX closed its Huntington operations in 2016.

The housing numbers explain why sellers here see a mix of owner-occupied homes and rentals. The 2020 census counted 46,125 housing units in the county, 13.5 percent of them vacant, and 39.5 percent of occupied units were rented. The encyclopedia lists a 63.7 percent home ownership rate and a median home value of $129,000, which is below the state's 73.9 percent ownership rate.

  • An owner who inherits a house in Huntington or Barboursville and lives elsewhere needs the sheriff to have a current mailing address, because tickets are mailed.
  • Landlords with Class 3 or Class 4 rental property pay a higher rate than owner-occupants, which raises the carrying cost of a vacant unit.

What are the Cabell County property tax rates for 2026?

For 2026 the Cabell County Assessor lists levy rates from 1.35520 to 3.46040 per $100 of assessed value, depending on class and location. The rates below come from the assessor's FAQ page.

AreaClass 2Class 3Class 4
City of Huntington1.675200.03.35040
Rural (outside a municipality)1.355202.710400.0
City of Barboursville1.730200.03.46040
City of Milton1.600000.03.20000

Class 2 covers owner-occupied homes and farms. Class 3 is other property outside a municipality, and Class 4 is other property inside one, as the West Virginia Tax Division defines them. A landlord in Huntington therefore pays double the Class 2 rate on the same house, because the assessor treats the rental as Class 4.

How is a Cabell County tax bill calculated?

A Cabell County bill equals the assessed value times the levy rate per $100, and the assessed value is 60 percent of market value. West Virginia Code 11-3-1 sets that 60 percent standard and fixes the assessment date at July 1.

Take a house worth $100,000 on July 1. Its assessed value is $60,000. At the rural Class 2 rate of 1.3552 per $100, the yearly tax is $813.12. At the Huntington Class 2 rate of 1.6752, the same house costs $1,005.12. These are illustrations built from the published rates, and a real ticket can differ because of exemptions or special levies.

The assessor's FAQ is blunt on one point: the assessor values property and does not set taxes. Levying bodies set the rates, and the office offers a tax estimator on its site so an owner can test a scenario before a sale.

Where do Cabell County property tax dollars go?

Schools take the largest share of Cabell County property tax. The state's classified valuations report for the 2024 tax year shows the following split of $111.7 million levied on all property in the county.

PurposeTaxes levied, 2024 tax year
State$364,880
County$30,416,390
Schools$69,152,044
Municipal$11,753,684
All purposes$111,686,998

By simple division, schools received about 62 percent of that total. The source is the Tax Division's 2024 report.

School excess levies have been a live topic. The encyclopedia reports that in 2023 the Cabell County Board of Education voted to stop funding parks and libraries from excess levy money, a circuit court blocked the move, and the state Supreme Court of Appeals sided with the board in February 2024.

How do you appeal a Cabell County assessment?

You appeal to the Cabell County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which must meet by February 1 each year. The assessor's FAQ gives (304) 526-9800 as the number to call during that period.

Under West Virginia Code 11-3-24 the board may adjourn after February 15 and must finish by the end of February. If it plans to raise your assessment, it has to give you at least five days of written notice. An owner who skips the board gives up the right to challenge that year's list, except through an appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals. The taxpayer carries the burden of a preponderance of the evidence.

  • Gather recent sale prices of similar homes nearby and any repair estimates that show condition problems.
  • Check the assessor's record for the wrong square footage, a demolished outbuilding or an incorrect class.
  • Appeals of a board order go to the Office of Tax Appeals, with a filing deadline of March 31 of the tax year under section 11-3-25b.

When are Cabell County taxes due and what happens if they are late?

Tickets go out on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half is due March 1. Paying either half before its date earns a 2.5 percent discount, according to the Tax Division's due dates page.

A first half that is not paid becomes delinquent on October 1, and a second half on April 1. Delinquent amounts earn interest at 9 percent per year. The Cabell County Sheriff's Tax Office collects the money at PO Box 2114, Huntington, WV 25721, telephone (304) 526-8672, and runs an online lookup.

Continued non-payment can lead to a lien sale. Under section 11A-3-2 the sheriff prepares a second list of delinquent land by September 10, and unredeemed tax liens are certified to the State Auditor on October 31 for sale at public auction. The statute adds $25 for the list and $10 per mailed notice. The owner can redeem by paying the sheriff before certification.

What filing deadlines and exemptions matter to Cabell County owners?

The homestead exemption takes the first $20,000 of assessed value off the bill for qualifying owners, and the filing window is July 1 through December 1. It applies to owners who are 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled and who have lived in West Virginia for two consecutive years, as section 11-6B-3 and the assessor's FAQ describe.

At the rural Class 2 rate, $20,000 of assessed value is worth about $271 a year. That is my arithmetic from the published rate. Other dates from the assessor:

  • Farm valuation applications: July 1 to September 1.
  • Business personal property returns: September 1.
  • Personal property returns for everyone else: October 1.

What does selling a Cabell County house with taxes owed look like?

The owner on July 1 owes that year's tax, and a sale does not erase it. Code 11-3-1 says taxes are paid by whoever owned the property on the assessment date, whether or not the bill carries that name, so a closing agent will normally pay any open ticket from the seller's proceeds.

A sale also carries a recording cost. Section 11-22-2 sets an excise tax of $1.10 for each $500 of value, retained by the county since July 1, 2025, plus an additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission may raise to $1.65. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without it. The clerk also collects a $20 fee on transfers for consideration. On a $100,000 sale the base rates produce $330, which is simple multiplication and excludes any local increase.

Paying the balance at closing keeps the parcel off a delinquent list, which matters for a Cabell County owner who is behind. Ask the sheriff's office for a payoff figure early, because interest at 9 percent per year keeps accruing until the taxes are paid.

What flood and age concerns affect Cabell County homes?

Low ground along the Mud River and the Ohio has flooded before, and buyers ask about it. The encyclopedia says the Mud River's banks have periodically overflowed into the lowlands, and the county's history includes the Ohio River flood of 1937. The assessor's link list points to the state's WV Flood Tool.

Railroad magnate Collis P. Huntington laid out the city in 1871 as the western terminus of the C&O, and industry followed, so parts of the county have housing stock well over a century old. An owner with repairs to make can ask a cash buyer to purchase as-is, which removes the need to fix anything before closing.

More questions about Cabell County, WV Property Tax Guide

Who sets property taxes in Cabell County?

Levying bodies set the rates. They are the county commission, the Board of Education and any city. The Cabell County Assessor only values property, and the assessor's own FAQ says the office does not set taxes.

What is the first-half property tax deadline in Cabell County?

September 1. Tickets go out on or after July 15, and a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay the first half before September 1. The first half becomes delinquent on October 1.

Can I sell my Cabell County house if I owe back taxes?

Yes. The unpaid taxes and interest are paid from your sale proceeds at closing. Call the Sheriff's Tax Office at (304) 526-8672 for a current payoff figure before you set a closing date.

How do I lower my Cabell County assessment?

Take your evidence to the County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which starts meeting by February 1. If you disagree with its order, you can appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals by March 31.

Who pays the transfer tax when a Cabell County house sells?

The grantor, meaning the seller, pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without it having been paid. State law sets $1.10 per $500 plus a county tax that starts at 55 cents per $500, and the county may raise that amount.

Martinsburg mattered to both armies in the Civil War because the main line of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad ran through it. Control of the town changed hands many times, especially before the Battle of Gettysburg in July 1863, and afterward it stayed mostly under Union control.

Berkeley and Jefferson counties voted in 1863 to join West Virginia. Virginia sued, and in 1871 the U.S. Supreme Court decided Virginia v. West Virginia and upheld the transfer. How is Berkeley County property assessed under West Virginia law?

The county assessor values property, and the sheriff bills and collects the tax. As of July 1 each year, ownership, use and value are set for the next calendar tax year. The State Tax Division says county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State all levy property tax.

The state constitution creates four property classes:

  • Class I: intangible personal property and certain farm personal property, with nothing currently taxed.
  • Class II: owner-occupied homes used only as a residence, and farmland used for agriculture.
  • Class III: property outside a municipality not in Class I or II.
  • Class IV: property inside a municipality not in Class I or II.

An investor who buys your owner-occupied house and rents it moves it out of Class II, so the tax can change after the sale.

When can you protest a Berkeley County assessment?

You protest to the county commission sitting as the board of equalization and review. That board begins meeting on February 1 each year and must adjourn by February 28, and your protest must be filed before that year's taxes are due.

How big is Greenbrier County and where do the towns sit?

Greenbrier County is the second-largest county in West Virginia, with 1,025 square miles in the southeastern part of the state. The Allegheny Mountains form its eastern edge and separate it from Virginia. Elevation runs from about 1,550 feet near Alderson to 4,360 feet at Grassy Knob in the northwest, according to the West Virginia Encyclopedia.

Lewisburg is the county seat. Ronceverte and White Sulphur Springs are the other two cities, and the towns are Alderson (partly in Monroe County), Falling Spring, Quinwood, Rainelle and Rupert, with Fairlea as a census-designated place. Much of the north and west is public land in the Monongahela National Forest or privately held forest and coal land, Wikipedia notes.

Three magisterial districts, Eastern, Western and Central, replaced ten older ones in the 1990s. The ten historic names, such as Anthony's Creek, Blue Sulphur and Meadow Bluff, are still used as tax districts. A parcel's tax district appears on the ticket.

What does the Greenbrier County economy depend on?

Resort tourism, health care, education and retail make up most of the employer list. The encyclopedia names the 2023 largest employers as the Greenbrier Hotel Corporation, the county school system, Greenbrier Valley Medical Center, the West Virginia School of Osteopathic Medicine and Walmart.

Older industries have shrunk. Meadow River Lumber Company, organized at Rainelle in 1910, once ran the largest hardwood manufacturing plant in the world, and in 2021 only 80 county residents worked in coal. How does the Greenbrier County assessor value a house?

The assessor appraises all property as of July 1 and is required to visit every parcel of real estate at least once every three years, although values are meant to track the market each year. The county's description says the land and personal property books must be finished by January 30 and handed to the Board of Equalization and Review by February 1.

By March 3 the assessor certifies assessed values to the city and town recorders, school board, State Board of Education and county commission. Those levying bodies use the values to lay their rates, and the sheriff then prints tickets from the certified rates. The office's own wording is that assessors determine values and the levies set by the bodies determine revenue.

State law sets the standard. Section 11-3-1 requires assessment at 60 percent of true and actual value, defined as the price the property would bring if voluntarily offered for sale, and it forbids using a forced-sale price.

The state due dates still apply. Delinquent taxes carry 9 percent annual interest, with the first half turning delinquent on October 1 and the second half on April 1, per the Tax Division.

What happens to a delinquent Greenbrier County parcel?

The sheriff publishes a list and the parcel can end up at a tax lien auction run through the State Auditor. Under section 11A-3-2, a second list of land still delinquent on September 1 is prepared by September 10, and unredeemed liens are certified to the Auditor on October 31.

The statute adds $25 to each listed item for publication and $10 per certified-mail notice. A listed owner can pay the sheriff before certification and come off the list. After certification the owner, or a lienholder, can still redeem by paying the Auditor before the sale. The statute also says a failure to receive the mailed notice does not undo a conveyance, so an owner with an outdated mailing address carries real risk.

What costs come with selling a Greenbrier County house?

Taxes for the year belong to whoever owned the property on July 1, and the deed carries a transfer tax. Under section 11-22-2, the recorded deed is taxed at $1.10 per $500, with an added county tax of 55 cents per $500 that the commission may raise to $1.65, plus a $20 transfer fee. The seller pays unless the buyer takes the deed without it.

A separate statute, section 8A-12-21, lets a county that has a farmland protection program add a further transfer tax of up to $1.10 per $500. Greenbrier has a Farmland Protection Board listed among its agencies, so ask the county clerk whether that extra tax applies to your sale.

For a $128,900 sale, the base rates of $1.65 per $500 come to roughly $426 (258 units of $500). That is my arithmetic and leaves out any county increase or farmland tax.

They can take longer, because a house with an estate or a flood history adds steps. The county lists an Estate Services office and estate forms among its agencies, which is the starting point when an owner has died and a deed must eventually be signed.

The encyclopedia records a deadly flood in 2016 along the Meadow River, devastating Rupert and Rainelle, while Howard Creek ran through White Sulphur Springs and the Greenbrier grounds. A seller near those waterways should expect questions about repairs, and an as-is cash sale skips the repair negotiation.

Owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled can claim a $20,000 reduction in assessed value under section 11-6B-3, and applications are due to the assessor by December 1. The county assessor's calendar gives April 30 as the last day to pay without penalty. State law makes the second half delinquent on April 1, and 9 percent interest runs from the delinquency date.

Yes. The assessor's calendar says appeals on value must be completed by January 31, and the Board of Equalization and Review hears appeals in February by appointment. Appeals from its order go to the Office of Tax Appeals.

Does a Greenbrier County seller owe the tax for the whole year?

The owner on July 1 is liable for that year's taxes under state law. In practice a closing agent pays any open balance from the seller's proceeds.

File an application with the assessor by December 1. You must be 65 or older, or certified permanently and totally disabled, and have lived in West Virginia for two consecutive years.

Where is Fayette County and what does the land look like?

Fayette County is in south-central West Virginia, just north of Beckley, with Fayetteville as the county seat. It covers about 668 square miles of high plateau, bordered by Sewell Mountain on the east and the Kanawha Valley on the west. The New River cuts a deep gorge through the middle and joins the Gauley at Gauley Bridge to form the Kanawha, according to the West Virginia Encyclopedia.

Neighbors are Nicholas, Greenbrier, Summers, Raleigh and Kanawha counties. The West Virginia Turnpike (Interstates 64 and 77) crosses the western part, and U.S. 19 crosses the New River Gorge Bridge, which the encyclopedia calls the county's chief landmark. Other routes include U.S. 60 and state routes 16, 39, 41 and 61.

The county's incorporated places are Fayetteville, Oak Hill, Mount Hope, Ansted, Gauley Bridge, Meadow Bridge, Pax and Thurmond, with Montgomery and Smithers shared with other counties. Local government uses three magisterial districts: New Haven, Plateau and Valley. A parcel on the plateau and a parcel in a river town can sit in different districts, so the district name on the tax ticket is worth knowing.

How did Fayette County's history shape its housing?

Coal and the railroad built most of Fayette County's older towns, and the decline of coal emptied some of them. The Chesapeake and Ohio Railway finished its line through the New River Gorge on January 29, 1873, and the county's population grew from 6,647 in 1870 to 60,377 in 1920. It peaked at 82,443 in 1950, then fell as mines closed.

The encyclopedia says the gorge, once crowded with mining towns, is now almost empty of residents, and that road building pulled the county away from the river and rail line onto the plateau. The 2025 estimate is 38,165 people, down 5.8 percent from the 2020 count.

That history leaves a county where population has dropped for decades, yet where visitors keep arriving. Sellers here are often dealing with a house in a small town, a lot outside any municipality, or an inherited property whose owners live out of state. Each of those leads to the same practical question: who pays the tax ticket until the deed changes hands.

Outdoor tourism is the county's growth story, and the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve anchors it. The National Park Service reports 1,811,937 recreation visits in 2024, with visitors spending an estimated $95.5 million in the surrounding region, which supported 948 jobs. The park was redesignated in December 2020, and whitewater rafting on the New and Gauley rivers, rock climbing, biking and fishing bring visitors.

What are the Fayette County property tax deadlines and penalties?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, and each earns a 2.5 percent discount if paid on or before that date. Nine percent annual interest starts when a half becomes delinquent, which is October 1 for the first half and April 1 for the second, as the state due dates page confirms.

Fayette adds a local warning: taxes still unpaid on April 30 are subject to publication, and publication brings extra fees. The county tells owners to contact the office for cut-off dates on delinquent properties.

State law then runs a clock. Section 11A-3-2 has the sheriff prepare a second list of delinquent land by September 10. Liens still unredeemed are certified to the State Auditor on October 31 and sold at public auction for at least the taxes, interest and charges. A person can redeem before certification by paying the sheriff, and after certification by paying the Auditor, any time before the sale.

How much of Fayette County's tax goes to schools?

How do you challenge a Fayette County assessment?

Challenge it before the County Commission acting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets starting February 1. Property is assessed as of July 1 at 60 percent of true and actual value under section 11-3-1, so a challenge is really an argument about what the house would have sold for on that date.

The board can adjourn after February 15 and must adjourn by the end of February. An owner who never applies at that meeting cannot revisit the list for that year except by appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals, and the deadline for that appeal is March 31. Anyone facing a higher value gets at least five days of written notice and a chance to speak, under section 11-3-24. The assessor's office at 100 Church Street handles real estate questions at 304-574-4239 or 304-574-4240.

Section 11-6B-3 sets the rule and requires two consecutive calendar years of West Virginia residence. The county tax page says the application period is July 1 through December 1, that it covers a primary residence only, and invites anyone 64 or older to contact the assessor.

A seller who already holds the exemption should say so when a buyer, or a title agent, asks about prorating the year's tax. The statute ties the exemption to the claimant, so a buyer would need to qualify on their own.

What does selling a Fayette County house with taxes due involve?

A title agent pays unpaid taxes from the seller's proceeds, and the deed transfer carries its own tax. Under section 11-22-2, recording a deed costs $1.10 per $500 of value plus a county tax of 55 cents per $500, which the commission may raise to $1.65, and a $20 fee on a transfer for consideration. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without payment.

For a $95,700 house, the base rates add up to $1.65 per $500, which comes to about $317 (192 units of $500). That is my arithmetic, and the county may charge more, so check with the clerk.

Time matters most when a parcel is close to April 30 publication or the September list. A cash purchase can close in days and settle the open ticket, which keeps the property off the delinquent list.

Do rental owners in Fayette County owe anything besides property tax?

Fayette County runs a hotel and motel occupancy tax through its tax department. It is due by the 15th of the month after collection, with a $15 late penalty, a 2.5 percent penalty for the first delinquent month and 1.5 percent for each month after. The county's page says no later payment is accepted until earlier delinquencies are paid in full.

Whether a particular house rented to guests counts is a question for the tax department, and a seller who has been renting near the park should ask before closing so no occupancy tax balance is left behind.

Who do I pay property tax to in Fayette County?

The Fayette County Sheriff's Tax Office at 100 Church Street in Fayetteville, or by mail to P.O. Box 509, Fayetteville, WV 25840. The phone number is 304-574-4219, and online payment is available.

When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?

October 1 for the first half and April 1 for the second half. Interest of 9 percent per year then applies, and taxes unpaid on April 30 are subject to publication with added fees.

Can I sell a Fayette County house that has unpaid taxes?

Yes. The tax balance, plus any interest, is normally paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the sheriff's office for a current payoff amount before you commit to a date.

How do I apply for the Fayette County homestead exemption?

Apply at the Fayette County Assessor's Office between July 1 and December 1. You must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, and the exemption covers a primary residence only.

What is the deadline to appeal a Fayette County assessment?

Start with the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets from February 1 and finishes by the end of February. Appeals of its decision to the Office of Tax Appeals are due March 31.

Why is Hancock County so small, and where are its towns?

Hancock County is the smallest county in West Virginia, with 88 square miles at the very top of the Northern Panhandle. The Ohio River forms its northern and western boundary, Pennsylvania lies to the east and Brooke County to the south, according to the West Virginia Encyclopedia. About 6 percent of the county's area is water.

Weirton, with 19,163 residents in 2020, is the largest city, and only part of it is in Hancock County. Chester, at the northern tip, had 2,214 people, and New Cumberland, the county seat, had 1,020. Newell and New Manchester are the larger unincorporated communities. U.S. 22 crosses the southern end, U.S. 30 clips the northern tip and state routes 2, 8 and 105 serve the river corridor.

For tax purposes the assessor divides the county into six districts: Butler Tracts, Chester, Clay, Grant/Newell, New Cumberland and Weirton. The assessor's page adds that part of Weirton lies in Brooke County, so a seller with a Weirton address should confirm which county's assessor and sheriff bill the parcel.

How did steel and pottery shape Hancock County?

Two companies set the county's twentieth-century economy: Homer Laughlin China at Newell and Weirton Steel. The encyclopedia says Homer Laughlin bought the Newell farm in 1902, built what became the world's largest pottery, and began making Fiesta tableware in the 1930s. Ernest T. Weir founded Weirton Steel in 1909, and by the 1950s it was the state's largest employer and taxpayer, with jobs for more than 13,000 people.

Ownership changed repeatedly after that. International Steel Group bought the mill in 2004, it passed to ArcelorMittal, and in 2020 Cleveland-Cliffs took it. In 2024 Cleveland-Cliffs announced it would close the Weirton plant, a move MetroNews reported as idling the plant with about 900 job losses.

The county's population peaked at 40,418 in 1980 and the 2025 estimate is 27,729, down 4.7 percent from 2020. Weirton's own population has fallen 32 percent from its 1960 high of 28,201.

New investment is also on record. Ground was broken in May 2023 on a 55-acre iron-air battery factory on former Weirton Steel land, owned by Form Energy and expected to generate 750 full-time jobs by 2028. Mountaineer Casino Racetrack and Resort is another major employer, and Tomlinson Run State Park draws visitors.

What are the housing numbers in Hancock County?

The median home value is $97,800, and 72.4 percent of households own their home. Those and the other figures below come from the encyclopedia's census summary and the 2020 census data on Wikipedia.

The share of residents 65 or older matters for tax planning, because it points to many owners who may qualify for the homestead exemption described below.

What are the Hancock County property tax classes?

West Virginia sorts every property into four classes, and the Hancock County Assessor explains them on its general information page. Class I is currently exempt. Class II is land owned, used and occupied by the owner solely for residential purposes, including mobile homes on land the owner does not own, plus farm land.

Everything else is Class III outside a municipality or Class IV inside one. Hancock County's municipalities are Chester, New Cumberland and Weirton. Class III and IV property is taxed at double the Class II rate, and Class IV also bears the municipal levy.

The page also says mobile homes or buildings on land owned by someone else are treated as personal property, and that farm land valued for farm use is appraised on fair rental value, which typically produces a lower figure than market value.

What are the 2026 Hancock County levy rates?

The assessor's 2026 levy page shows a Class II total of 1.34826 per $100 of assessed value in the table it displays, which lists no municipal levy. The components are below, taken from the Levy Rates page.

The assessor notes the tax bill is the levy rate times assessed value, normally 60 percent of market value. On a $100,000 house that means $60,000 of assessed value and about $809 a year at the Class II total. The homestead exemption removes $20,000 of assessed value, or about $270 at this rate. Both amounts are my arithmetic from the published rate.

Schools received about 69 percent of the 2024 levy. The state's classified valuations report lists these amounts for all property in the county.

What does the Hancock County Assessor handle?

The assessor values property and also collects several small county fees, at 102 North Court Street in New Cumberland, telephone (304) 564-3311. Its fee list shows a $3.00 building permit, a $2.00 mobile home decal, a $1.00 per page property record printout and a $3.00 dog license.

  • Personal property returns: all residents report taxable property owned on July 1, and the return is due between July 1 and October 1. The assessor warns that not filing can complicate vehicle registration renewals.
  • Business personal property: returns are due by October 1, and a business that fails to file forfeits appeal rights.
  • Farm use valuation: first-time applicants file between July 1 and September 1.
  • Homestead exemption: apply between July 1 and December 1 in the assessor's office. An owner who is 64 on or before the July 1 assessment date should apply so the exemption starts with the next year's taxes.

The assessor's site also offers a property search, sales records, tax maps, map cards and a tax estimator.

How do you appeal a Hancock County assessment?

Appeals go to the Hancock County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which opens by February 1. State law lets the board settle a valuation by approving an agreement signed by the taxpayer and the assessor, so a negotiated result is possible before any formal hearing.

Under section 11-3-24, the board cannot raise a value without five days of written notice, and it caps assessments at 60 percent of true and actual value. A taxpayer who fails to apply gives up that year's correction, aside from an appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals. The standard of proof throughout is a preponderance of the evidence.

What happens when Hancock County taxes go unpaid?

Unpaid real estate can end up in a lien sale, and the Hancock County Tax Office page has a heading for a Deputy Land Commissioner's Land Sale. The office is at 102 N. Court Street, with mail to P.O. Box 458, New Cumberland, WV 26047, and an online search is available.

The statewide schedule is first half due September 1 and second half March 1, with delinquency on October 1 and April 1 and interest at 9 percent a year. Under section 11A-3-2 the sheriff lists land still delinquent on September 1 by September 10, and unredeemed liens are certified to the State Auditor on October 31.

What does it cost to sell a Hancock County house?

The seller normally pays the transfer tax, and the closing agent settles any open tax ticket. Section 11-22-2 imposes $1.10 for each $500 of value plus a county tax that starts at 55 cents and can reach $1.65, along with a $20 transfer fee. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without it.

At the median home value of $97,800, the base rate of $1.65 per $500 comes to about $323 (196 units). That is my own multiplication, and any county increase would add to it. Since the owner on July 1 is liable for that year's tax under section 11-3-1, a seller who closes in the fall should ask the title agent how the second half is being handled.

The Hancock County Sheriff's Tax Office, at 102 N. Court Street in New Cumberland, with mail to P.O. Box 458. The telephone number is 304-564-3311, and an online search and payment site is available.

What is the Hancock County property tax rate?

The assessor's 2026 table shows a Class II total of 1.34826 per $100 of assessed value, with Class III and IV at double that. Class IV inside a city adds the municipal levy, so check the levy page for your district.

Is Weirton taxed by Hancock County?

Mostly, yes, but part of Weirton lies in Brooke County. Confirm which county's assessor and sheriff bill your parcel before you sell.

Who qualifies for the Hancock County homestead exemption?

Owners who are 65 or older, or certified totally and permanently disabled, with two consecutive years of West Virginia residence. It removes $20,000 of assessed value, and you apply at the assessor between July 1 and December 1.

Can I sell a Hancock County house with delinquent taxes?

Yes. Delinquent taxes and interest are paid from the sale proceeds. Contact the Tax Office at 304-564-3311 for a payoff figure, and do it before the September list is prepared.

Jefferson County by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts 58,546 people and 24,276 housing units in Jefferson County, which ranks 9 of 13 West Virginia counties here. Median home value is $324,500, which is 105% above the middle county in this West Virginia set. Households here earn a median $95,523; the middle West Virginia county is at $58,326. 21% of occupied homes are rented, which leaves 79% owner-occupied.

Where is Jefferson County, West Virginia, and why is its property tax different?

Jefferson County has far fewer people than Kanawha County, yet its Class II assessed value is close to Kanawha's. It was established on October 26, 1801, from Berkeley County, covers 212 square miles and has Charles Town as its seat. It borders Washington County, Maryland to the north and Loudoun and Clarke counties, Virginia, to the east and southwest.

The Potomac and Shenandoah rivers meet at Harpers Ferry. Charles Town and Ranson are the cities, and Bolivar, Harpers Ferry and Shepherdstown are the towns. U.S. 340 and West Virginia routes 9, 45 and 51 are the main roads. Growth here comes mainly from commuting to the Washington area, which is why values and bills look different from the rest of the state.

How does commuting affect Jefferson County homeowners and sellers?

Many residents live in Jefferson County and work in Washington or Northern Virginia, so demand follows the commute. The MARC Brunswick Line runs from Martinsburg into Washington, with West Virginia stops at Harpers Ferry (120 Potomac Street) and Duffields (5057 Flowing Springs Road). West Virginia riders pay a surcharge on top of the base fare, according to the MARC rider guide.

The county's character also comes from history. John Brown's 1859 raid on the federal armory at Harpers Ferry led to his trial at the Charles Town courthouse, and Jefferson County voted to join West Virginia in 1863. The county was also the first in the United States to start Rural Free Delivery, in October 1896.

Older properties in Harpers Ferry, Shepherdstown and Charles Town can come with preservation questions, aging systems and unusual lot lines. Sellers with a house like that often prefer a buyer who accepts it in present condition.

The county also has five magisterial districts, Charles Town, Harpers Ferry, Kabletown, Middleway and Shepherdstown, and census-designated places such as Shannondale, Shenandoah Junction and Middleway. Rural parcels outside Charles Town, Ranson and the three towns are Class III or Class II depending on use, while parcels inside a municipality that are not owner-occupied are Class IV. Check where your parcel sits before you compare a bill with a neighbor's.

How does the Jefferson County Sheriff run property tax collection?

The Sheriff's Tax Office at 110 N. George Street in Charles Town collects the tax but does not set the rate or value property. More than 46,000 bills are processed each year. Mail goes to P.O. Box 9, Charles Town, WV 25414, and the phone is 304-728-3220.

  • Real estate tax is due semi-annually, with a 2.5 percent discount for first-half payment by September 1 and second-half payment by March 1.
  • The office does not accept credit cards, and checks should show the tax ticket number.
  • Delinquent tax lists are published in the Spirit of Jefferson in May and September.
  • An online tax search and payment system is available, along with a payment portal run by Point and Pay.

The county page also says property is reappraised at least once every three years, and that the real property tax rate comes from the County Commission. Tax bills are mailed around mid-year.

What does Jefferson County's lack of an excess levy mean for owners?

The 2025 state levy report shows Jefferson County with no county excess levy: its county purposes levy of $20,020,050 is entirely current expense. Kanawha, Harrison and Marion counties all carry excess levies, which are voter-approved additions on top of regular rates.

That does not mean a Jefferson County bill is low. Voters can also approve school board excess levies, and higher home values mean a larger bill at the same rate. West Virginia's regular ceilings for Class II property inside a municipality add up to $1.00 per $100 of assessed value, and a $300,000 house assessed at 60 percent is $180,000, which is $1,800 at that ceiling before any school excess levy. Treat that as an illustration, not a quote, and confirm the actual levy with the sheriff.

For sellers, the higher the value, the more a late payment costs in interest at 9 percent a year, and the more a missed homestead filing matters. Owners 65 or older may exclude the first $20,000 of assessed value if they filed.

How do you appeal a Jefferson County assessment, and who sells delinquent property?

Challenges go to the County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which starts on February 1 and adjourns by the end of the month. The county's page says only that decisions on challenged assessments are made by the commission, so rely on the state rule for dates. An appeal from the board goes to the Office of Tax Appeals by March 31.

On delinquent property, the county page says a law passed in 2022 placed the sale of delinquent properties with the West Virginia State Auditor. A seller with unpaid tax should ask the Sheriff's Tax Office where the parcel stands before the lists are published in May and September.

If you want to avoid that process, a cash sale lets the title company pay off the tax at closing. We buy houses as-is across Jefferson County, from Charles Town and Ranson to Shepherdstown, and you can reach us at (424) 435-2326. There is no need to repair, clean out or stage the house first, and we will explain the written offer in plain terms.

What should a Jefferson County seller know about personal property and closing costs?

Real estate is only part of the Sheriff's job. Personal property tax on vehicles, boats, livestock, farm equipment and machinery is due September 1 and March 1, and paying it is a condition of renewing a vehicle registration with the state. If you are leaving the county, clear those bills so a registration is not held up later.

  • Delinquent personal property accrues penalties, and its delinquent list runs in May.
  • Real estate tax is separate and is paid at closing from proceeds when it is owed.
  • The county excise tax on a recorded deed is 55 cents for each $500 of value, under the transfer tax statute.
  • Transfers of $1,000 or less in value fall outside the definition of a taxable document.

Since the real property assessment is revisited at least every three years, a house you bought some time ago may carry a value that has moved. A reassessment notice can change what a buyer will pay in tax, so a seller should look up the current assessment before listing. A cash buyer will look at the property as-is and handle the paperwork with you.

More questions about Jefferson County, WV Property Tax Guide

When are Jefferson County property taxes due?

Real estate tax is due in two halves, September 1 and March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay each half by its date. Unpaid tax accrues 9 percent annual interest, with first-half tax delinquent October 1.

Does the Jefferson County Sheriff take credit cards?

No. The Sheriff's Tax Office says it does not accept credit cards, and payments can be made in person or by mail. An online payment portal is also listed.

How often does Jefferson County reappraise property?

The county assessor reviews real property at least once every three years under the state's triennial reassessment rule, and some properties more often.

Who sells delinquent tax properties in Jefferson County?

The county says a 2022 law moved sales of delinquent properties to the West Virginia State Auditor.

What is the Jefferson County homestead exemption?

Resident owners aged 65 or older can exclude the first $20,000 of assessed value from taxation. State law also covers owners certified permanently and totally disabled.

Where is Barbour County, West Virginia, and what is it like?

Barbour County sits on the Allegheny Plateau in north-central West Virginia, with Philippi as the county seat. It covers 342.9 square miles of mountainous country drained by the Buckhannon, Middle Fork and Tygart Valley rivers.

The Virginia legislature created the county on March 3, 1843, from parts of Lewis, Harrison and Randolph counties, and named it for the Virginia jurist Philip Pendleton Barbour. It borders Taylor and Preston counties to the north, Tucker and Randolph to the east, Upshur to the south and Harrison to the west. Laurel Mountain, the westernmost of the high Allegheny ridges, marks the eastern edge.

U.S. 119 and U.S. 250 run the length of the county, north to south, and U.S. 33 cuts across the southern tip. Philippi had 2,928 residents in 2020 and Belington, the second-largest town, had 1,804.

What is the history of Barbour County and Philippi?

Philippi was the site of what is generally considered the first land battle of the Civil War among organized troops, fought before dawn on June 3, 1861. About 3,000 federal troops under Col. Benjamin F. Kelley routed roughly 800 newly recruited Confederates. The Battle of Belington, or Laurel Mountain, followed on July 7 to 11, 1861.

Philippi's covered bridge, which carries U.S. 250 across the Tygart Valley River, was built by Lemuel Chenoweth in 1852 and is still the town's best-known landmark. The railroad reached Philippi on January 25, 1884. The last passenger train stopped there in 1956, and the line now carries only freight. The 1911 depot has been the Barbour County Historical Museum since 1979.

The county courthouse was completed in 1905. If you hold an older house in the county, a deed or survey may reference these historic roads and river bottoms, so keep the paperwork together for a buyer.

How does flooding affect houses in Philippi and Barbour County?

Philippi sits mostly on low bottomland along the Tygart Valley River, and it has flooded repeatedly. The most damaging flood came in November 1985, and the town has since adopted a floodplain management plan.

If you own a house in a river bottom, take these steps before you sell:

  • Ask your insurer or title company whether the parcel is in a mapped flood zone.
  • Collect any repair invoices from past water damage.
  • Disclose past water in the basement or crawl space to every buyer.
  • Find out whether the lender on a financed buyer will require flood insurance.

Flood questions slow down financed purchases, since lenders and insurers have to sign off. A buyer paying cash does not need a lender's approval, though a careful buyer will still look at the risk.

What drives the Barbour County economy?

Natural resources have defined the local economy: coal, gas and timber, plus family farms in the valleys. Hardwood logging boomed at the start of the twentieth century, and second- and third-growth timber is still cut each year. Oil reserves were mostly depleted early in the century.

Coal output fell from a 1948 high of 3,895,803 tons to just over 2.3 million tons in 2021, then rose to more than five million tons by 2025, making Barbour the state's ninth-leading coal county and one of the fastest-growing. That swing shows how closely household finances here can follow commodity cycles.

Alderson Broaddus University, a Baptist institution that began as Broaddus Institute in 1909 in Philippi, closed permanently in 2023. Owners near the former campus who counted on university-related demand should ask a local agent or appraiser how the closure has affected their street.

How is West Virginia property tax assessed, and how does Barbour County fit in?

West Virginia assesses all real and tangible personal property, with limited exceptions. As of July 1 each year the ownership, use and value of property are fixed for the next calendar tax year. The county assessor values your property, and the county sheriff bills and collects the tax.

The state constitution divides property into four classes:

  • Class I: intangible personal property and certain farm personal property. Nothing is currently taxed in this class.
  • Class II: owner-occupied residential property used only for residence, and farmland used for agriculture by its owner or a bona fide tenant.
  • Class III: property outside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.
  • Class IV: property inside a municipality that is not in Class I or II.

That matters at a sale. A house you live in is Class II, while a rental or vacant house falls in Class III or IV depending on where it sits, so the tax can change after the buyer takes ownership. Property tax is levied by county boards of education, county commissions, municipalities and the State.

West Virginia Code 11-6B-3 exempts the first $20,000 of assessed value of a homestead from ad valorem tax. The owner must be 65 or older, or certified as permanently and totally disabled, and must use and occupy the home only as a residence.

The owner must also have been a West Virginia resident for the two consecutive calendar years before the tax year. An owner who receives a similar exemption in another state is not eligible.

If you plan to sell, the exemption matters less to you than to the buyer. A new owner under 65 will not carry it over, so the tax bill may rise. Mention that to a financed buyer's agent so there is no surprise at the first tax ticket.

The office also posts summer satellite days at places such as Meadowbrook Mall, the Clarksburg Senior Center and several fire stations, so people in Shinnston, Lost Creek or Spelter do not always need to drive downtown. Filing is also available online through the state's SmartFile system.

What filing dates matter to Harrison County owners?

The assessor's 2026 filing season runs from July 1, and the key dates differ by form. Individual personal property returns are due between July 1 and October 1, and business personal property returns and farm exemption applications between July 1 and September 1. Homestead exemption applications can be filed from July 1 through December 1 to take effect for the following tax year.

Tax tickets themselves follow the state schedule. They are issued on or after July 15, the first installment is due September 1, the second March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies before those dates. Unpaid first-half tax becomes delinquent on October 1 and second-half tax on April 1, with 9 percent annual interest.

West Virginia's homestead exemption removes the first $20,000 of assessed value for an owner who is 65 or older or certified permanently and totally disabled, and who meets the residency rule. A seller who qualifies should confirm the exemption was actually filed, since a missed filing means a higher bill on a house about to be sold.

How do Harrison County owners appeal a valuation?

Talk to the Assessor's Office first, then take the dispute to the Harrison County Commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets from February 1 and finishes by February 28. The board can reduce a value that exceeds 60 percent of true and actual value, and it must give written notice at least five days before raising one.

If the board rules against you, the next step is the Office of Tax Appeals, with a petition due by March 31 of the tax year. Missing the February window waives the right to argue that year's list. Dispute over whether a home is Class II or Class IV is handled separately with the assessor and the Tax Commissioner.

Evidence that works is concrete: a recent appraisal, a repair estimate for a damaged structure, or sales of similar homes. For a house you plan to sell soon, an appeal is often not worth the effort unless the value is clearly wrong, because the new owner will be assessed on the next cycle anyway.

What happens to unpaid tax and how does a cash sale handle it in Harrison County?

The sheriff certifies unpaid real estate tax for sale, and the State Auditor, not the sheriff, now runs the lien sale. An older tax lien sale FAQ posted on the county site says the sale was held between October 17 and November 24. Marion County's sheriff, a neighbor, explains the change in the law from the Legislature and a certification deadline of October 31.

Because rules shifted, call the Sheriff at 304-624-8685 before you assume anything about timing or redemption cost. A seller who owes tax can often clear it through closing: the title company obtains a payoff and pays it from the proceeds. The county excise tax on a recorded deed is 55 cents for each $500 of value under the transfer tax statute.

We buy houses in Harrison County as-is, so a house in Clarksburg that needs a roof, has a tenant, or carries back taxes does not need to be fixed first. Call or text (424) 435-2326 for a written cash offer.

Do minerals and mobile homes change a Harrison County tax picture?

They can, because the Assessor's Office keeps separate divisions for mobile homes and for oil, gas and minerals. A mobile home may be assessed through its own desk at 304-624-8517, and oil and gas or mineral matters go to 304-624-8523. The state also runs its own appraisal process for oil and gas royalties.

When you sell, ask the assessor and your title company whether any mineral interest is tied to the parcel and whether it carries its own assessment. Deeds do not always say, and a buyer will want a clear answer. Cash buyers are generally fine with houses where title questions like this need work, and we check before we make an offer.

West Virginia's four classes also matter. Class II covers owner-occupied residential property used exclusively as a home. Property in a municipality that does not qualify, such as a rental house in Clarksburg, falls in Class IV, and property outside a municipality falls in Class III. Those classes have higher regular ceilings than Class II.

More questions about Harrison County, WV Property Tax Guide

When are Harrison County property taxes due?

Half is due September 1 and half March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount applies if you pay before each date. Taxes unpaid after October 1 (first half) or April 1 (second half) are delinquent and accrue 9 percent yearly interest.

Where is the Harrison County Sheriff's tax office?

It is at 229 South 3rd Street, Clarksburg, WV 26301, and the phone for taxes due is 304-624-8685. Online payment is also offered.

When can I apply for the homestead exemption in Harrison County?

Eligible homeowners apply between July 1 and December 1 to receive the exemption for the following tax year. It covers the first $20,000 of assessed value for owners 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.

What is the deadline to appeal a Harrison County assessment?

Protest to the county commission sitting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which starts February 1 and ends by February 28. An appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals is due March 31.

Can I sell a Harrison County house that has back taxes?

Yes. A title company can get a payoff for the unpaid tax and pay it from the sale proceeds at closing.
